India Aiming to Host 2036 Olympics, Commonwealth Games in 2030, Says Speaker Speaking at the Major Dhyan Chand Stadium on the birth anniversary of former President APJ Abdul Kalam, the speaker felicitated Indian athletes for their historic performances at the Asian Games. Emphasising national pride, the address noted that out of eighty-five medals, thirty-eight were won by women athletes, including eleven gold medals. Historic milestones were highlighted, including the women's hockey team breaking a forty-four-year gold medal drought, victories in cricket, kabaddi, archery, shooting, boxing, wrestling, sailing, soft tennis, and mixed martial arts. Key government initiatives such as the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, Khelo India, and extensive sports infrastructure development were outlined alongside enhanced monthly allowances and international coaching support. Highlighting that young athletes aged fifteen to seventeen demonstrated exceptional promise, the speaker noted plans for talent identification among children aged five to fifteen. Reaffirming national goals, the address declared ambitions to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and the 2036 Olympic Games while fostering a global sporting hub.
